interactions.before:
• Hormonal contraception: Sugammadex may reduce contraceptive efficacy; advise women to use an additional non-hormonal method of contraception for 7 days (oral contraceptives) or 5 days (implants).
• Toremifene, fusidic acid: May displace rocuronium or vecuronium from sugammadex complex; monitor for recurarisation.
• Re-administration of NMBAs: If rocuronium or vecuronium is required within 24 hours of sugammadex 2 mg/kg or 4 mg/kg, consider a benzylisoquinolinium NMBA (e.g., atracurium or cisatracurium) if a shorter onset NMBA is not essential. Suxamethonium can be given immediately. If rocuronium is given within 6 hours of sugammadex 2 mg/kg, onset may be delayed and duration shortened. If vecuronium is given within 24 hours of sugammadex 4 mg/kg, onset may be delayed and duration shortened.
interactions.after:
• Hormonal contraception: Sugammadex may reduce contraceptive efficacy. If an oral contraceptive was taken on the day of sugammadex administration, follow the contraceptive’s missed-dose instructions. For non-oral hormonal contraception, use an additional non-hormonal method for the next 7 days and follow the product advice.
• Toremifene, fusidic acid: May displace rocuronium or vecuronium from sugammadex complex; monitor for recurarisation.
• Re-administration of NMBAs: If rocuronium or vecuronium is required within 24 hours of sugammadex 2 mg/kg or 4 mg/kg, consider a benzylisoquinolinium NMBA (e.g., atracurium or cisatracurium) if a shorter onset NMBA is not essential. Suxamethonium can be given immediately. If rocuronium is given within 6 hours of sugammadex 2 mg/kg, onset may be delayed and duration shortened. If vecuronium is given within 24 hours of sugammadex 4 mg/kg, onset may be delayed and duration shortened.

dosing.before:
• Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) or history of Myocardial Infarction (MI): Loading dose 180 mg orally, then 90 mg twice daily. After 12 months, for patients with a history of MI and high risk of atherothrombotic events, 60 mg twice daily.
• Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD): 60 mg twice daily.
• Renal impairment: No dose adjustment for mild, moderate, or severe impairment. Contraindicated in dialysis patients or estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <15 mL/minute/1.73 m².

dosing.after: Named UK ticagrelor product emc 100957: ACS 180 mg oral loading, then 90 mg twice daily for 12 months unless clinically indicated otherwise. Qualifying prior MI ≥1 year with high atherothrombotic risk: 60 mg twice daily under the product selection criteria. Not licensed solely for PAD. Product ASA maintenance recommendation: 75–150 mg/day unless specifically contraindicated; selected post-PCI high-bleeding-risk patients may discontinue ASA after 3 months per the product protocol. No renal dose adjustment; dialysis/eGFR <15 is not a listed contraindication. Severe hepatic impairment contraindicated; caution in moderate hepatic impairment. Paediatric safety/efficacy not established. Prior ischaemic stroke requires the product-specific duration/evidence discussion, not an invented PAD contraindication.

contraindications.before:
• Active pathological bleeding or history of intracranial haemorrhage (ICH).
• Severe hepatic impairment.
• Concomitant use with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, atazanavir, indinavir, telithromycin, nelfinavir, saquinavir).
• Concomitant use with aspirin maintenance doses >100 mg daily.
• History of ischaemic stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA) in patients with PAD (MHRA alert, 2017).
• Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients.
contraindications.after: Hypersensitivity; active pathological bleeding; history of intracranial haemorrhage; severe hepatic impairment; concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Aspirin >100 mg/day and dialysis are not formal contraindications in the named UK SmPC. Assess bleeding risk and product-specific aspirin recommendations separately.

indication_oneliner.after: Prevention of atherothrombotic events in adults with ACS or qualifying prior MI at high risk; not standalone PAD.
